delegation_note: On 2026-10-07 Nitin Rajput delegated the open owner decisions ('self review and decide recommended option') on top of the signed basis 'do everything as recommended'. Entries whose why starts with [delegated 2026-10-07] were decided under that delegation. The two cart finance keys (cart.credit_balances, cart.erpnext_invoices_legal) are accepted on that basis; Airpay Finance was not consulted. No skip reason is pre-accepted: accepted_reasons is absent on purpose, and the owner adds each needs-owner reason with its Stage B count after the rehearsal. Any edit after the Stage B rehearsal changes the sha256 and is a re-approval event.
basis: owner instruction: do everything as recommended

framework.adr_accepted.why: [proposed] ADR-032 asks Nitin to accept the shared map, legacy tables as the archive, the id rule and a CLI guard instead of a feature flag. Owner instruction is to accept as recommended.

framework.reader_flags_default.why: [proposed] CLAUDE.md sections 5 and 13: every new user-visible surface ships behind a default-OFF flag. The import never flips a flag.

framework.reader_flags_airpay_at_cutover.why: [instruction] The history readers are turned ON for the Airpay customer at cutover only after Nitin has reviewed the visual evidence. A flag flip is always Nitin's call, never the importer's or a script's.

framework.decisions_file_owner.why: [instruction] Nitin owns and signs this file.

framework.decisions_change_after_rehears.why: [instruction] Any edit after the Stage B rehearsal changes the pinned sha256, so cutover cannot run until Nitin re-approves and the new hash is pinned.

framework.cutover_rollback.why: [instruction] The RDS snapshot taken before the import is the only rollback at cutover. --purge-feature stays a rehearsal tool.

framework.purge_feature_on_production.why: [instruction] --purge-feature is not allowed on production (it is already refused when bizlms_production = 1).

framework.legacy_table_privacy.why: [instruction] Not decided here. Export-and-anonymise versus drop-after-audit gets its own ADR after sign-off. Until then the legacy tables are untouched (ADR decision 2) and the privacy gap stays recorded.

framework.inline_key_mode.why: [proposed] The ADR keeps it off by default and needs an amendment to allow it. Revisit only if Stage B shows the window is too short.

framework.protect_imported_history.why: [rule 1] No recommendation on block versus soft-delete. Nothing is lost: delete and retype actions on imported rows are blocked (and cascade to the new tables), shipped with each importer.
framework.protect_imported_history.source: ADR-032 lines 608-609; mapping doc classroom fix 7, program fix 10, learningplan fix 9, evaluation fix 7

framework.file_rehome_copies.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] File copies made by file_rehome in finalise() (org logo, cohort descriptions, learning-plan cover, classroom logo, program logo) are copy-only, insert-only and idempotent; the originals are never touched. Each importer declares its exact source and target areas through a marker instead of core_writes, so --purge-feature stays available. A purge leaves the copies, and every run report counts them. {files} is watched for every importer without the marker.
framework.file_rehome_copies.source: ADR-032 Side-effect safety 3; owner decision 2026-10-07 IDN-04 (delegated)

framework.protect_imported_history_pendi.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] An admin may unenrol an imported enrolment that has no completion, progress or attendance, on an active path, classroom or program. Every row that carries history stays blocked. The BizLMS row stays in the legacy archive. On a learning path the learner's converted course enrolments are not removed (BizLMS removed them); the admin is shown which remain.
framework.protect_imported_history_pendi.source: ADR-032 decision 2; framework.protect_imported_history; mapping doc sections 15 to 17; owner decision 2026-10-07 LRN-10 (delegated)

framework.imported_rows_on_admin_pages.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] Imported entities that other rows reference (orgs, roles, courses and enrolments, plans, programs, classrooms, evaluation forms and their responses, rules) show on the admin pages that manage them. Imported history and log rows that nothing references (orders, ledger, credits, e-mail log, requests, recompletion resets, HRMS sync runs, login days, transcripts) show only when the feature's imported-history flag is ON, which Nitin flips after reviewing the visual evidence. HRMS sync runs get sentientia.users.imported_sync_history.

Airpay Finance was NOT consulted, so 'accepted' records the delegated recommendation and is not a Finance sign-off. The credit journal and balances import as frozen, admin-only history behind the default-OFF flag sentientia.cart.imported_credits.enabled. Nothing in Sentientia honours, spends, pays out or writes off a balance; native checkout never reads the credit tables. April 2026 rehearsal copy: 0 credit bookings, 0 ledger rows, 0 holders, INR 0. If Stage B shows any non-zero balance, the count and total go to Airpay Finance before cutover, including how a holder's erasure request is handled. A Finance answer is a re-approval event.

cart.erpnext_invoices_legal.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] Nitin delegated this decision ('self review and decide recommended option'). Airpay Finance was NOT consulted, so 'accepted' records the delegated recommendation and is not a Finance sign-off. Stored ERPNext numbers import as references only: ERPNEXT-<id>, status legacy_external, shown to order admins as 'Issued in ERPNext as <number>' behind the default-OFF flag sentientia.cart.imported_orders.enabled, with no link-out. Sentientia never issues an invoice number for a BizLMS sale: the legal invoice is the one the registered invoicing system issued, and a serial is never re-issued. April 2026 rehearsal copy: 0 invoice rows and no ERPNext connector configured. Finance confirms the legal record only if Stage B shows rows.

learningplan.user_startdate.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] [fail closed] BizLMS never writes local_learningplan_user.startdate (April: 0 values). Any value found blocks the feature until its origin is understood.
learningplan.user_startdate.source: mapping doc section 17; owner decision 2026-10-07 LRN-09 (delegated)

learningplan.stalled_nudge_scope.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] [rule 2] The automatic stalled-path nudge never targets imported BizLMS enrolments or archived paths. An admin can still nudge those learners by hand.
learningplan.stalled_nudge_scope.source: mapping doc section 17; owner decision 2026-10-07 LRN-11 (delegated)

evaluation.open_forms.why: [proposed] Still-open forms import as ARCHIVED and manual, so no observer can invite anyone and nobody can answer by accident.

evaluation.multichoicerated.why: [proposed] Weighted multichoice questions import as plain multichoice. The weights stay in the legacy tables.

evaluation.sp_anonymous_subject.why: [proposed] Supervisor-evaluation forms that were anonymous hide the subject too.

evaluation.legacy_anonymous_linkage.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] Originally an owner instruction (2026-09-30); the scope was widened on 2026-10-07. Anonymous answers import anonymous (userid 0, no subject). The legacy tables still link them to people and are not altered here. Two more links count as part of the same gap: the import's map, where the 'assign' sub-row and the anonymous response share one completion id, and the completion-ordered ids of implied assignments. The separate legacy-table privacy ADR must cover the map and the id order as well as the legacy tables, and it must be accepted before any legacy evaluation table is anonymised or dropped.
evaluation.legacy_anonymous_linkage.source: mapping doc section 18; ADR-032 open decision 5; owner decision 2026-10-07 EV-19 (delegated; first recorded as an owner instruction on 2026-09-30)

evaluation.trainer_feedback_form_names.why: [rule 3] No recommendation. Each trainer feedback form keeps its BizLMS name. The trainer link stays in local_classroom_trainers.feedback_id, so nothing is lost and no trainer name is added to an anonymous form.

evaluation.imported_forms_read_only.why: [rule 1] The documents call this an owner decision. Imported forms are read-only: delete and retype of answered questions are refused on them.

evaluation.sticky_anonymity.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] A form that ever collected an anonymous answer (its flag, or any completion with anonymous_response 1) imports every completion with userid 0 and no subject, including completions BizLMS stamped named (2). This pools the anonymous answers so none can be singled out by subtracting the named ones, and it matches identity_protected(), which hides every respondent of such a form anyway. The legacy table keeps the person link (evaluation.legacy_anonymous_linkage). April: no form is affected.
evaluation.sticky_anonymity.source: mapping doc section 18; owner decision 2026-10-07 EV-16 (delegated)

evaluation.tenant_editor_fallback.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] A BizLMS form whose path, stored root (costcenterid) and parent classroom give no tenant imports pathless (cross-tenant callers only, reported). It is never filed under the tenant of the user who last edited it. BizLMS showed such forms to site admins only, and a guessed tenant would show named answers to admins who never saw them. April: no form affected.
evaluation.tenant_editor_fallback.source: mapping doc section 18; owner decision 2026-10-07 EV-TENANT (delegated)

request.pending.why: [proposed] Legacy pending course and path requests stay actionable in the approvals inbox (a person must still decide, and auto-expire and escalation skip imported rows). Classroom, program and certification requests are always read-only. Rule 2 would have closed them as history, but its own exception applies because the document says otherwise.
request.pending.source: mapping doc section 23 line 2784; section 19 lines 2525-2526, 2563

request.pending_stale.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] A legacy pending course or path request whose requester is deleted or suspended, or whose item no longer exists, imports as history (pending, no approver), like classroom and program requests. Approving it would enrol and message an account that has left, or point at nothing. Admins still see it in All requests.
request.pending_stale.source: mapping doc section 19; owner decision 2026-10-07 COMMS-R1 (delegated)

request.pending_classroom_program.why: [proposed] Pending classroom and program requests stay history. rm::decide refuses item types other than course and path.

request.certification.why: [proposed] Certification requests stay unmapped (item_type certification, legacy id kept) until an owner entity exists (gap G3).
request.certification.source: mapping doc section 23 line 2785; section 21 G3

request.decided_route.why: [proposed] Decided legacy rows carry route 'admin', not a new 'legacy' value.

request.hidden_rows.why: [proposed] Rows BizLMS hid (deleted components, deleted or suspended requesters) are shown to admins in Sentientia. Rule 3 would have filtered them, but the document proposes show.
request.hidden_rows.source: mapping doc section 23 line 2787; section 19 line 2567

request.tenant_basis.why: [proposed] A request's tenant is the requester's current root. The source stores no tenant.

request.pending_approver.why: [proposed] Legacy pending approvers come from Sentientia routing (supervisor, manager, default approver), not a named L&D admin.

request.comments.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] Request comments are folded into decision_note. BizLMS has no writer for local_request_comments, so it is expected to be empty. If it holds rows, preflight blocks for the owner, because who could see them is unknown and the note is shown to the requester. A decision on an imported row appends to the folded note and never replaces it.
request.comments.source: mapping doc section 19; owner decision 2026-10-07 COMMS-R4 (delegated; why extended, value unchanged)

ratings.invalid_rows.why: [proposed] Invalid rating rows (NULL, 0, out of range, unknown area, missing item or user) are skipped and reported. They stay in the legacy table.

ratings.blank_reviews.why: [proposed] Blank reviews import but are hidden by the reader.

ratings.deleted_users.why: [proposed] Ratings, reviews and reactions of deleted users are kept.

ratings.show_dislike_counts.why: [rule 3] No recommendation. BizLMS showed a dislike count beside the thumbs-down (local/ratings/lib.php lines 56-60), so the reader shows like and dislike counts (status 1 and 2 only), behind the default-OFF reaction flag.
ratings.show_dislike_counts.source: mapping doc section 20 lines 2663-2664, 2706; BizLMS local/ratings/lib.php lines 43-60

ratings.certification_area.why: [proposed] Ratings under the certification area, and any unknown area, are skipped and reported (reason unknown_area) until a target entity exists.

gaps.other_tag_areas.why: [proposed] Classroom, learning plan and evaluation tag instances are counted in preflight and left where they are. No BizLMS plugin is uninstalled (ADR decision 2), so they are not deleted.
gaps.other_tag_areas.source: mapping doc section 21 G5 line 2722; section 7 lines 536-538

gaps.classroom_program_skill_tags.why: [proposed] Skill and level tags on classrooms and programs stay in the legacy tables.

gaps.notification_sender_parity.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] BizLMS sends course_enrol, learningplan_enrol and manager copies of course_complete, and Sentientia has no sender for them. They are built behind default-OFF flags. Turning them on for Airpay at cutover is Nitin's call after UAT evidence. Welcome and learner completion e-mails already exist natively.
gaps.notification_sender_parity.source: mapping doc sections 11 and 21; owner decision 2026-10-07 COMMS-N7 (delegated)

gap.orphan_enrol_instances.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] Without the BizLMS enrol_classroom, enrol_program and enrol_learningplan code, enrolments on those instances can no longer be managed (no unenrol, suspend or expiry handling), while core still grants course access through any enabled instance whether or not its plugin is on disk (require_login uses enrol_get_enrolment_end, which checks only instance and enrolment status). Convert each such user_enrolments row to a manual enrolment in the same course, keeping status, timestart and timeend, and record the original instance in the legacy map. Each fully converted BizLMS instance is then disabled (enrolments.bizlms_instances_after_verify). Verify at the Stage B rehearsal that every affected learner keeps access.
gap.orphan_enrol_instances.source: ADR-032 open decision (gap G6); mapping doc section 21; owner decision 2026-10-07 XC-G6-WHY (delegated; why corrected, value unchanged)

enrolments.bizlms_instances_after_verify.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] Core grants access through any enabled instance whether or not its plugin is on disk (require_login -> enrol_get_enrolment_end), so leaving the BizLMS instances on makes a Sentientia unenrol or suspend ineffective. An instance is disabled (status 1, never deleted, prior status kept in a trail) only when every (user, course) pair on it keeps an access window at least as wide through manual enrolments, proved per pair against core's rule. An instance with a regression or an unsettled needs-owner row stays enabled. One UPDATE reverses it.
enrolments.bizlms_instances_after_verify.source: mapping doc section 21 (G6); owner decision 2026-10-07 CRS-01 (delegated)

enrolments.disabled_instance_row_status.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] [rule 3] A row on a disabled BizLMS instance gives no access today. It converts as a suspended manual enrolment: the record is kept, no access is added, and an admin can reactivate it. 0 rows on April.
enrolments.disabled_instance_row_status.source: mapping doc section 21 (G6); owner decision 2026-10-07 CRS-02 (delegated)

enrolments.disabled_only_manual_instance.why: [delegated 2026-10-07] [rule 1 + rule 2] A course whose only manual instance is disabled gets a new enabled one beside it. The admin's disabled instance is untouched and learners keep today's access. 0 courses on April.
enrolments.disabled_only_manual_instance.source: mapping doc section 21 (G6); owner decision 2026-10-07 CRS-03 (delegated)
